clinician.trajectory_summary: A 63-year-old male with uncontrolled hyperglycemia and recent SARS-CoV-2 infection (immunocompromised state) presented with weakness, a fall, and right-sided facial droop. Initial non-contrast CT demonstrated advanced sinusitis. CTA performed after admission showed progression of sinusitis with abnormal gas in multiple foci including the skull base, left occipital condyle, and soft tissues adjacent to the clivus—findings highly suggestive of invasive fungal infection with bone involvement. Based on radiological findings of potential Mucor and skull base involvement, fiberoptic nasal endoscopy was performed, which demonstrated sinusitis consistent with invasive sinusitis due to mucormycosis. Pathology from the endoscopy revealed non-septate branching hyphae, confirming mucormycosis. The patient subsequently underwent endoscopic debridement, which demonstrated Mucor on the carotid wall, confirming the invasive nature of the infection affecting the skull base region. The constellation of imaging findings (abnormal gas in skull base and soft tissues adjacent to clivus), pathological confirmation of mucormycosis (non-septate branching hyphae), and procedural findings (Mucor on carotid wall during debridement) in the context of immunocompromise (uncontrolled diabetes and recent SARS-CoV-2 infection) establish the diagnosis of osteomyelitis of the clivus secondary to mucormycosis.

Pathology specifically identified non-septate branching hyphae consistent with Mucor species, not Aspergillus (which has septate hyphae)

remaining_uncertainties: Explicit documentation of clivus osteomyelitis in imaging or clinical reports (the diagnosis is inferred from CTA findings of abnormal gas and soft tissues adjacent to clivus combined with pathological confirmation of mucormycosis, but no source record explicitly states 'clivus osteomyelitis')
Specific antifungal treatment regimen initiated, dosing, and clinical response
Patient's clinical outcome and hospital course following diagnosis and treatment
Laboratory confirmation of uncontrolled diabetes mellitus (glucose, HbA1c values at admission)
